sources: docs/prepared-show-spec-2026-11.md (the answer key: names, the baseline, the scenes)
docs/status/console-checklist.md on main (the shop section, and the dLive and SQ re-check rows)

tests.title: Companion on the Yamaha Rivage PM5 (DSP-RX): the family's first run — from source, about 3 min (almost all of it over HTTP)
tests.answers: the module thread; the Rivage's Companion row (first run on the Yamaha family)
tests.expect: the module names this family from the driver's own name ('yamaha', YamahaTargetDriver.name); scenes by NUMBER with no place to resolve to, so the desk's own recall announcement carries number null and the number on screen in scene_number — scene_current must follow it and must NOT read 0 (that was #342's second site, fixed today); levels are exact dB on an RCP desk, so fader_ch1 is the desk's own figure
tests.record: the module's SHA; every variable read, with its value; the connection status string; MIDI Bridge's log over the block (writes, echoes, scene events with number and name, and the 400s); Companion's log for the dylanmaudio connection
tests.safety: Every write is on SAFE9 (Input 9: no source patched, no output patched, no main assign) or is a scene recall of DMA TEST's own scenes. Nothing in DMA TEST is patched to an output and no main assign is on, so no write reaches audio on any of these desks. The block ends by recalling BASE, which puts SAFE9 and Input 8 back as found. The module never writes a level to a desk whose dB law MIDI Bridge has not measured: it refuses and says so.

steps.prompt: Page 11 'Shop check' must be imported into Companion ONCE before the first desk (not per desk): Companion -> Buttons -> Import, choose blocks/shop-check.companionconfig from the module repo, and put it on page 11. It carries 14 buttons: row 0 SAFE9's fader and mute, row 1 scenes by place, row 2 scenes by number (including list B and a list the desk hasn't got). It references the existing dylanmaudio connection by id, so the import should map it with nothing to choose. If page 11 is taken, import it anywhere and change the page number in every curl below. Row 0's 'MUTE off' button carries NO feedback: until 4 Nov it carried the same mute feedback as 'MUTE on', so both lit red whenever ch 9 was muted (seen on the Quantum). A page imported before that fix shows the old look -- cosmetic, and it must not fail the mute ask, which is about 'MUTE on'.

steps.text: CLAUDE, the build (nothing is sent). Companion runs this module from source through a dev-module symlink — /Users/dylanmitrovich/companion-dev-modules/dylanmaudio -> /Users/dylanmitrovich/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio — and the connection's moduleVersionId is "dev", so whatever is in the repo's dist/ IS the module. Check all three: (a) git -C "/Users/dylanmitrovich/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio" rev-parse --short HEAD  → wants 69635f4 or any later commit on topic/avantis-yamaha, and RECORD what it reads; 69635f4 is the last commit that changed src/, so a later HEAD is docs or these blocks and changes no behaviour; (b) git -C "/Users/dylanmitrovich/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio" status --short  → wants empty (an uncommitted change means dist/ and the SHA do not describe each other); (c) find "/Users/dylanmitrovich/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio/dist" -name '*.js' -newer "/Users/dylanmitrovich/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio/src/bridge/bridgelink.ts" | head -1  → wants a line (dist newer than src; if empty, run corepack yarn build in that checkout and nothing else). There is no package to import and no version to bump: 1.1.93 is the version on every build of this line, so the SHA is the identity. Record the SHA, not the version.

CLAUDE, reach — READ THIS BEFORE THE DESK IS BOOKED. Companion and its dev module are on THIS Mac; the Yamahas are at the MacBook station. MIDI Bridge's Client API binds 127.0.0.1 ONLY in this build and refuses anything else: dlive_midi_server.py says so in its own comment ('Binds to 127.0.0.1 only'), and shared/control_api._host_ok refuses a Host whose name is not loopback OR whose PORT is not the bridge's own (apps/midi-bridge/tests/test_client_api_http.py asserts the 403 for 'another port'). LAN mode with a token is in the spec (§4) and is NOT in this build. So there are exactly two ways to run this block, and one of them has to be chosen in advance: (a) an SSH tunnel from this Mac, forwarding the SAME port number the MacBook's bridge listens on — ssh -N -L 8765:127.0.0.1:8765 <macbook> — with this Mac's own bridge NOT holding 8765 at that moment, and Companion left pointing at 127.0.0.1:8765 (no Companion change at all); or (b) Companion and this repo installed on the MacBook. (a) is cheaper and uses the SSH link RESEARCH already keeps. A tunnel on a different local port will 403 on every request: the port in the Host header is checked. I have read this in the code but NOT measured it against a running bridge (ours was down when I wrote this) — so prove it in one command before the desk time: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: 127.0.0.1:9999' http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/info wants 403, and the same without the -H wants 200.

CLAUDE, the desk and the gate (nothing is sent). curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/info and read the console block. Wants: it names the Rivage PM5 (and its model, DSP-RX or the desk's own productname); verified_on_desk true (V applied in A — if it is false the look still RUNS, read-only: every write is refused with the module's own sentence, and that refusal is itself a pass for this step, recorded as 'gate shut'). Two things here, both new. First, the Yamaha is verified PER MODEL: V is 5c06d69f + 3da0c542 on DEV: Yamaha driver's word after A, and the DM7's is a different commit. Second, the bridge can only say which model it is once the desk has answered, so verified_on_desk can flip from false to true WHILE Companion is connected. The module handles that as of today (69635f4) by re-reading the block from the SSE console event; if this block is run on an older build the connection would sit refused all session. Read the block again after the model appears and record both readings. NEW TODAY, and worth knowing if V is applied mid-session: the module re-reads this block from the bridge's SSE `console` event, so a desk that becomes verified while Companion is connected starts being driven WITHOUT a reconnect. Before today it would have refused for the rest of the session.

CLAUDE, the connection's own words (nothing is sent): curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/connections | python3 -m json.tool — the dylanmaudio row's status. Wants category "ok" on a verified desk. On an unverified one it reads "MIDI Bridge is driving a <desk>; this module version drives a dLive only": copy it word for word, it is the evidence for 'gate shut'. This is the same sentence the operator would read on Companion's Connections tab, so nobody has to look at the screen for it.

CLAUDE, the cold state, read over HTTP (nothing is sent). Run: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/name_ch1/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/name_ch8/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/fader_ch1/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/fader_ch5/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/mute_ch8/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/linked_ch11/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/partner_ch11/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/width_ch11/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current_name/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/connected/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/gets_missed/value; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/unsupported_gets/value; Against DMA TEST (prepared-show-spec §Must 2, 6, 8, 11, 13): name_ch1 ZEBRA1, name_ch8 NARWHAL8, fader_ch1 "0.0", fader_ch5 "-20.0", mute_ch8 true, scene_current 1 (the show is stored with Scene 1 last, so it loads at BASE), connected true. scene_current_name is EXPECTED EMPTY on every desk here: the module only knows scene names from an imported dLive show file, and it does not read the bridge's scene list yet (audit §4 item 4) — empty is a pass, not a fail. linked_ch11 / partner_ch11 / width_ch11 are the stereo pair: whichever of the two forms the desk reports, and EMPTY where the desk cannot say — empty is the right answer there, never false (550c3ba). A Yamaha's level is an integer in hundredths of a dB and the wire value IS the dB, so fader_ch1 is the desk's figure and fader_lv_ch1 may be empty. Names are 8 characters on some models: if name_ch8 comes back cut, record exactly what it reads — that is the desk's answer, not a module fault.

CLAUDE, the writes, over HTTP. SAFE9 (Input 9) has no source or output patched and no main assign, so none of this reaches audio. In order, 2 s apart: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/0/press (SAFE9 -20 dB); curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/1/press (0 dB); curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/3/press (MUTE on); curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/4/press (MUTE off); curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/2/press (-inf, as found). Read back after each: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/fader_ch9/value, curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/mute_ch9/value. FADER_DB FIRST (the Quantum, 4 Nov): the three fader presses reach the desk only if the bridge declares its dB law for THIS desk, so read the flag before pressing: curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/info | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['capabilities'],d['console'].get('model'),d['console'].get('verified_on_desk'))". capabilities.fader_db FALSE -> the three fader presses are an EXPECTED refusal: nothing is sent, no TX in MIDI Bridge's log, fader_ch9 does not move, and the evidence is in COMPANION's log (not the bridge's), one line per session: "Levels aren't sent to a <family>: MIDI Bridge hasn't verified its dB law, so a dB here wouldn't land where it says." Record that line and the flag and score the step pass-with-note. TRUE -> the faders must move, and a non-move is a real fail. The flag is the bridge's own: _capabilities() withholds fader_db unless Codec.fader_db_verified AND, where the family lists its verified models, this desk's model is one of them -- on the Quantum (SD7Q-Q1) it read false while verified_on_desk read true. Then the scene BY NUMBER — this desk numbers its scenes, so the module sends scene_number and strips the place (a place-based recall on a by_number desk is the #55 class of wrong recall): curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/1/press (No 2.00, ALLZERO). The proof of the recall is scene_current: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value → 2. And here it IS the desk's word: since 073dd1d the module applies nothing locally on a desk that NUMBERS its scenes, because a number is not a place (9.99 is not the ninth snapshot), so this variable moves only when the desk's own scene event arrives. Before that commit it went blank on every recall and the desk's echo filled it in a few ms later. Then, for the channels, RECORD curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/fader_ch2/value and curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/mute_ch8/value rather than failing on them. Nothing is captured for what a Yamaha broadcasts after a recall, so this run is what records it: note whether they arrive at all, and how long after the press. Then the refusal: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/3/press (No 9.99, which no scene has) — MIDI Bridge answers 400 desk_state, the module logs it and does NOT retry, and nothing reaches the desk.  Then the scene that only exists on these desks: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/2/press (No 2.50, HALF, prepared-show-spec §Must 15) and curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value → 2.5. Watch the bridge's scene event for this one: on a desk with no places it carries number null and scene_number 2.50, and scene_current must still read 2.5. The press endpoint is POST and answers 204 whether or not a button is there (checked against this Mac's Companion, 3 Nov: POST /api/location/99/9/9/press → 204, GET → 404), so a 204 proves NOTHING. The proof of every press is the variable read-back above and MIDI Bridge's log.

CLAUDE, #342: the loaded scene on CONNECT, not after a recall. Companion keeps the last value it was given across a disconnect, so reading scene_current while the link is down proves nothing — the test has to be a fresh connect with the desk NOT on scene 1. So: recall ALLZERO first (curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/1/press), confirm curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value reads 2, then make the module reconnect. The two ways of reconnecting are NOT equivalent, and only one of them tests this (found 5 Nov, in the module's code): the operator TOGGLES the dylanmaudio connection off and on in Companion's Connections tab (about 5 seconds). That destroys the module's instance and builds a new one, so its ConsoleState starts empty and scene_current can only come from the snapshot. Restarting MIDI Bridge does NOT do that: in bridge mode the module never clears its state on a reconnect — nothing calls state.reset(), and refetchState only APPLIES what the new snapshot carries — so the module still remembers the 2 it had and the read would pass against a completely empty bridge mirror. Use the toggle. Then, BEFORE pressing anything: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value must read 2 again — read out of the bridge's cold snapshot at GET /api/v1/state. 0, blank, or 1 is #342 unfixed. A MIDI Bridge restart is still worth doing as its OWN check, and record it as that: it shows the lane re-hellos, the connection row goes Connecting then OK, and no variable is destroyed by a reconnect. It says nothing about the snapshot. Then CLAUDE puts the desk back: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/0/press (BASE — No 1.00), then the proof is curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/scene_current/value → 1, and RECORD curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/fader_ch2/value and curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/dylanmaudio/mute_ch8/value without failing on them, as above. BASE also puts SAFE9 back, whatever the writes above left it at.

CLAUDE, the list that isn't there: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/4/press (No 1.00 in list B). A Rivage declares no scene lists, so the module REFUSES this press itself and logs "Nothing recalled: this console keeps one scene list, so there is no list \"B\" to recall from." Wants: that line in Companion's log, and NOTHING on the wire for it — the bridge would have answered 400 bad_intent, and a refusal that arrives after the press is a button that silently did nothing. Then curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/2/5/press (list C) for the same answer.

steps.question: On Companion's Connections tab, the dylanmaudio row is green/OK (not Connecting or an error)?
Press page 11's 'SAFE9 MUTE on' button: does that button go red while SAFE9 is muted, and back when you press 'MUTE off'?

steps.prompt: CO: the module's SHA; every variable read above with its value; the connection status string word for word; MIDI Bridge's log over the block (each write, each echo, each scene event with its number and name, and the refusal of 9.99 -- which is in COMPANION's log, not the bridge's: the bridge refuses a number not in the list before it touches the desk, so there is no TX, and the module's line reads "Bridge rejected scene: desk_state (...)" (or scene_unavailable if the snapshot list is still being read). Grep Companion's log for "Bridge rejected"); and Companion's own log for the dylanmaudio connection over the block (Settings -> Log, or ~/Library/Logs/companion). Anything the operator said.
